name: Tetramelic Monodactyly

criteria.description: Presence of monodactyly affecting all four limbs
Radiographic evidence of absent or hypoplastic digits in all limbs
No evidence of associated craniofacial or visceral malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of monodactyly in all four limbs confirmed clinically and radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be inconclusive.

searchTerms: one finger or toe on each limb
single digit on hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of multiple digits on hands and feet
searchTerms: multiple absent digits on hands and feet
lack of several fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Hypoplasia of metacarpal and metatarsal bones
searchTerms: short bones in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected limbs
searchTerms: decreased range of motion in arms or legs
one limb shorter than the other

common.symptomName: Soft tissue contractures around affected digits

occasional.symptomName: Mild muscle atrophy in affected limbs
searchTerms: slight muscle loss in affected arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Nail hypoplasia or absence on affected digits
searchTerms: small or missing nails on fingers or toes

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones due to limb malformations
searchTerms: delayed walking or movement due to limb issues

rare.symptomName: Transient skin erythema over affected limbs
searchTerms: brief skin redness over arms or legs

rare.symptomName: Mild sensory deficits in distal limbs
searchTerms: slight numbness or tingling in hands and feet
mild loss of sensation in distal limbs
reduced feeling in fingers and toes

imaging: Radiographs showing monodactyly with absent or hypoplastic phalanges and metacarpals/metatarsals
MRI may show soft tissue contractures and muscle hypoplasia
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
Genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic associations
other: Clinical examination revealing symmetrical monodactyly of all four limbs

distinguishingFeatures: Variable number of digits affected, often asymmetrical
Presence of short, webbed fingers rather than single digit
Usually involves central digits rather than complete monodactyly

redFlags: Presence of associated craniofacial or visceral malformations
Progressive limb deformities or worsening contractures
Signs of neurovascular compromise in affected limbs
references: Kumar S et al. Tetramelic monodactyly: clinical and radiological features. J Pediatr Orthop. 2018.
Smith J et al. Limb malformations: differential diagnosis and management. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2020.
